title: SQL plans, connection pools, and transaction size
outcome: Investigate a slow service without assuming more threads or caching is the first fix.
useCase: Slow list endpoints and connection exhaustion incidents.
benefits: Repairs the bottleneck rather than hiding it.
drawbacks: Representative measurement and safe database change plans take effort.
cue: Find the wait before adding capacity.

trace.title: Request queue
trace.detail: A request can wait for a connection, a row lock, a slow query, or an external service. Low CPU does not prove spare useful capacity. Trace waiting time separately from execution time.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Trace request arrival → pool wait → SQL/lock wait → row fetch → DTO mapping → response. Measure each boundary before changing a limit.

For a transaction that calls a slow provider between writes, show how many requests can hold connections while waiting. Move delivery intent into an outbox when a later external effect is acceptable.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A larger pool can overload the database. SQL logs can expose values. A query that is fast on 10 rows may use a different plan on a million.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Investigate a slow service without assuming more threads or caching is the first fix. Explain one example and one failure.
